entry.summary: No visa for a tourist visit of up to 30 days.
entry.pre_arrival: Accommodation booked for the whole stay. Flights run only through New Zealand, so New Zealand's entry rules apply too.

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: Niue has one official currency, the New Zealand Dollar (NZD). The bank cannot change currency. Most shops and hotels accept credit cards however there is typically a surcharge applied. There are no ATMs in Niue. You can withdraw cash from the bank and some shops. Before you leave, ask your bank if your cards will work overseas.

laws.rule: Penalties for carrying or using even small amounts of illegal drugs are severe. They may include fines and prison sentences.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: Same-sex relationships between men were decriminalised in Niue in May 2024. Niuean society is conservative. Avoid public displays of affection.
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: You’ll need a local driver’s licence to drive in Niue. Your overseas driver’s license can be used to apply for a local license at the Niue Police Station. You can only drive vehicles covered by the class on your licence. For example, with an Australian car licence you can drive a car but not a motor scooter.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Standards of dress and behaviour are modest. Be careful not to offend. Sunday is a day of religious observation in Niue. This means very few businesses operate on a Sunday. By law, water-based tour operators are not permitted to operate on Sundays. Whilst there are no laws that prohibit swimming or sightseeing on Sundays, people are expected to be discreet in their choice of activities.
